result.reason: All three items form a continuous chain discussing why the mishna omitted the trefah distinction (item 1), Ravina's answer that the mishna follows Rabbi Shimon who exempts trefot from reshit ha'gez (item 2), and the Gemara's challenge about deriving from teruma instead (item 3) — all of which are directly discussed in the 'Trefah Not Listed' prose under heading 0.

Both items discuss the tzon-tzon gezeirah shavah linking reshit ha'gez to ma'aser and the exclusion of tereifa via 'whichever passes under the rod,' which is precisely what the 'Terumah Linkage Rejected' prose describes as the actual mechanism of Rabbi Shimon's derivation after the terumah link is rejected.

All three items enumerate the shared features of reshit ha'gez and ma'aser (zecharim, tmeim, bimrubim, merachem, adam, pashut, lifnei ha'dibur) that make it logical to derive reshit ha'gez from ma'aser rather than bechor, which is precisely what candidate 1 'Reshit HaGez & Ma'aser' describes in its prose.

All three items enumerate the shared halakhot between reshit ha'gez and bechor (yatom, shelakchu, shutfut, matanah, bifnei kohen, bikdushah, mechira) and conclude they are more numerous — exactly what candidate 0's prose describes in detail, before candidate 1 moves on to the pashut resolution.

The passage directly states 'pashut mipashut adif lei' — the exact phrase discussed in the 'Pashut as Key Factor' section prose, which explicitly explains why the shared 'ordinary animal' identity of ma'aser and reshit ha'gez overrides numerical connections to bechor.

All four items form a continuous chain — Rav Ḥisda's gezeirah shavah from Job, the objection to derive instead from the bechor context, the baraita expanding that prohibition, and the resolution via 'titen lo' — which is precisely the sequence described in heading 0's prose.
The passage directly states the goat hair exclusion due to lack of 'geizah' (shearing), which is precisely what the 'Goat Exclusion' prose describes as 'ba'inan geizah v'leika.'

The passage directly discusses who holds the narrow interpretation of geizah (Rabbi Yosei) and his concession for normal methods (modeh Rabbi Yosei b'midi d'orchei), which is precisely what the 'Rabbi Yosi & Verbs' prose section describes.
The passage directly presents Rabbi Yehoshua ben Levi's 'davar harauy l'shirut' principle, which is precisely what the 'Priestly Garment Test' section prose describes and analyzes.

The passage directly addresses the purpose of the gezeirah shavah and the school of Rabbi Yishmael's teaching about hard wool being exempt from reshit ha'gez, which is precisely what the 'Hard Wool Exemption' section's prose discusses.

All six items cover exactly the content described in the 'Rabanan-Rabbi Yosi Debate' prose: the two conflicting baraitot on washing sheep, the lo kashya resolution, the leket/katzir analogy, the kuli Rabbi Yosi clarification, the modeh Rabbi Yosi b'midi d'orchei principle with Rav Acha's statement, and the malbinot betzalim mishna proof — all of which the candidate 1 prose explicitly discusses in sequence.

All three items together form the continuous Gemara discussion of Beit Hillel's reasoning via the word *asuyot*, including Rav Kahana's derivation, the challenge about firstborn and gifts, and Rav Ashi's reformulation — exactly what the 'Asuyyot Analysis' prose describes.
The baraita presents Rabbi Yishmael son of Rabbi Yosi citing his father's opinion of four sheep derived from Exodus 21:37, which is precisely what heading 0's prose describes.

All three items — Rabbi's preference for Rabbi Yosei, the objection about ein hachra'ah shelishit machra'at, and Rabbi Yochanan's explanation of the prophetic tradition — are exactly the content described in the 'Rabbi Prefers Yosi' prose, which explicitly covers all three points in sequence.
